claims.text: Dermatology AI fails in dark-skin, non-cancer settings.
claims.poster_quote: Dermatology AI fails in dark-skin, non-cancer settings.

claims.paper_evidence: Patients present with more pigmented skin, and with a disease burden dominated by inflammatory and infectious conditions (eczema, tinea, impetigo, scabies) that are largely absent from cancer-centric training data.
claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that dermatology AI models are trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data and fail in settings where patients have darker skin and non-cancerous conditions like eczema or tinea. This supports the claim.

claims.text: Disease shift may matter more than skin tone underrepresentation.

claims.reason: The paper discusses that disease distribution shift contributes more to the generalization gap than skin tone underrepresentation, directly supporting the claim.

claims.text: Models trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data are deployed where patients have darker skin and non-cancerous conditions like eczema or tinea.

claims.reason: The paper explicitly states that models trained on light-skinned, cancer-focused data are deployed in settings with darker-skinned patients and non-cancerous conditions.
